Package io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley

@NullMarked package io.github.tobyjamesclements.parsley
Parsley: causal delivery order for Kafka Streams processors. A single package whose public surface is a concise, topology-level API modelled on Kafka Streams; the low-level processor decorator that powers it is package-private internal machinery.

Three pillars

  • Causal broadcast. Every record carries the producer's causal dependencies in a header; a consumer holds a record in a changelog-backed buffer until its own frontier dominates those dependencies, then delivers it — so a topology of Kafka Streams processors sees causally related events across topics in the order they actually happened, not merely in per-partition order. The classic broadcast/receive/deliver vocabulary and where each lives in this package is spelled out in ParsleyCausalBroadcast's Javadoc. See CausalClock for the wire contract and the edge operations below for talking to a Parsley topology from plain Kafka clients.
  • Coordination-free joins. There is no membership, no epoch, and no join barrier: a new application simply starts consuming, its replay self-gates into causal delivery order through the ordinary hold-back queue, and its truthful stamps make its outputs correctly gated everywhere from the first emission. Parsley has no configuration keys at all; startup fails if any parsley.* key is present.
  • Schema handling. A held record's key and value are (de)serialised with the Serde registered for its own source topic, never the buffer's internal changelog topic, so topic-scoped serdes — Avro plus Schema Registry TopicNameStrategy in particular — resolve the correct subject even for a record held across a schema change. A record that becomes undecodable while buffered (e.g. an incompatible registry change) fails the task fast rather than being silently dropped or forwarded on an unproven causal premise.

Entry point

Three roles mirroring Kafka Streams — StreamsBuilder / Topology / KafkaStreams:
  • CausalStreamsBuilder — declare the one causal stage: stream(...) one or more source topics, .process(supplier) to bind them to a causal-decorated processor, .to(...) to declare its sink(s); .build() produces a CausalTopology
  • CausalTopology — the built causal topology, ready for new CausalStreams(topology, props)
  • CausalStreams — the runtime: wraps the underlying KafkaStreams instance, and owns graceful causal drain on close()

Edge operations

To talk to a Parsley topology from plain Kafka clients, stamp and propagate causal dependencies directly with CausalClock:
  • using — bind a resolver (topic name → stable Kafka UUID, resolved internally through the given Kafka client configuration) and start accumulating a consumer-side frontier
  • observe — fold a consumed record's dependencies and own position into the accumulator
  • stamp — attach the accumulated dependencies to an outbound ProducerRecord
  • merge — combine dependency sets for a fan-in

Internal protocol modules

Internally the implementation is organised as layered protocols, each presented in the module style of Cachin–Guerraoui–Rodrigues (Introduction to Reliable and Secure Distributed Programming): requests in, indications out, properties guaranteed. The channels module (ParsleyChannels) adapts Kafka topic-partitions into the reliable FIFO channels classical causal broadcast assumes; the causal-broadcast module (ParsleyCausalBroadcast) is Birman–Schiper–Stephenson causal delivery over those channels; the gossip module (ParsleyGossip) disseminates clock progress as null messages so completeness keeps flowing through non-emitting paths. Two Parsley-wide deviations from the textbook presentation apply to every module, stated once here:
  • Indications are pulled, not pushed. Deliveries come back as ordered return values rather than through an upcall, because Kafka Streams' threading is synchronous. Same semantics, pull style.
  • The sender's clock increment is performed by the broker. In Birman–Schiper–Stephenson the sender increments its own vector entry at send; here the increment is the broker's offset assignment, learned asynchronously from producer acknowledgements. This is why an outbound stamp cannot include the record's own coordinate.

Naming convention

Every public type is named Causal*; the one exception is ParsleyOwnOutputInterceptor, public only because Kafka instantiates producer interceptors reflectively and is not public API. Package-private machinery is named Parsley*, except implementations of a Parsley* seam interface, which are named for their backing: KafkaTopics implements ParsleyTopics, and StoreBackedBufferStore / StoreBackedCandidateIndex / StoreBackedForwardedIndex implement their Parsley* store interfaces over any Kafka Streams KeyValueStore.

Key value types

  • CausalClock — the causal requirements stamped on a record (what the consumer must have observed before the record may be delivered). Its serialised size grows with the number of relevant topic-partitions and counts against Kafka's message.max.bytes. Topic-UUID resolution is an internal detail of using/ builder — there is no separate public resolver type to construct or manage
  • Class
    Description
    CausalBufferDeserializationException
    Thrown when a held record's key or value cannot be deserialised from the buffer store on the forward path (drain or propagate) — typically because the registry state for its subject changed after the record was buffered (e.g. the writer schema id was deleted, or a redeployed reader schema is incompatible).
    CausalClock
    A vector clock (Fidge 1988; Mattern 1988, "Virtual Time and Global States of Distributed Systems") over causal coordinates: a set of (topic, partition) → offset entries, indexed by channel — the topic-partition — rather than by process, a stated variant of the classical form (Kafka's partition is the stable, durable axis a process identity is not).
    CausalClock.Builder
    Builder for CausalClock.
    CausalCoordinateException
    A CausalDeliveryException anchored to a single source coordinate — the (topic, topicId, partition, offset) quartet identifying the record the failure is about, exposed for operator diagnostics.
    CausalDeliveryException
    Base of every exception Parsley's causal machinery throws out of a processing task.
    CausalPendingAckException
    Thrown by the crossing-wait primitive when a pending own-output acknowledgement times out, fails, or the wait is interrupted.
    CausalProcessedStream<K,V>
    A causal stage bound to its processor, ready to declare sink(s) with CausalProcessedStream.to(String) and then terminate the topology with CausalProcessedStream.build().
    CausalStream<K,V>
    One or more causal source topics, ready to feed a single causal-decorated processor with CausalStream.process(ProcessorSupplier).
    CausalStreams
    The causal application runtime: a Facade (GoF) over the Kafka Streams instance a CausalTopology runs as, and the causal machinery a plain KafkaStreams doesn't know about — graceful causal drain on shutdown — behind the one simple start/close lifecycle below.
    CausalStreamsBuilder
    Builds a CausalTopology: exactly one causal stage — a set of source topics feeding a causal-decorated processor and forwarding to one or more sinks.
    CausalTopicRecreatedException
    Thrown on the record and stamping paths once Parsley's topic-identity watch has detected that a causal topic was deleted (or deleted and recreated) while this member ran.
    CausalTopology
    The immutable causal topology CausalProcessedStream.build() produces: the single declared stage's source topics, processor, sink(s), and partitioner.
    CausalVectorClockResolutionException
    Thrown at ingest when an inbound record's parsley-causal-clock header is present but cannot be decoded into a vector clock — a corrupt or truncated header, or one written in an unsupported wire version.
    ParsleyOwnOutputInterceptor
    The producer-side half of the ownOutputs clock (D2): publishes every acknowledged send to a declared sink topic into this instance's ParsleyOwnOutputRegistry, from which the stream threads fold coordinates into ParsleyChannels.acknowledge(Uuid, int, long) before each stamp.
